meta.titre: Tenses and Moods: choosing the right verb form from the clues
meta.sous_theme: Choosing the tense or mood that the sentence requires
tags: O Level French - tenses and moods

sections.contenu_markdown: Your uncle in Bafoussam tells the family how the lights went out during a football match and how everybody kept talking in the dark. To tell that story he must choose between what happened, what was going on and what had happened before. French does the same thing with different verb forms. In Paper 1 a blank asks you to pick the tense or mood that the other words demand, and in Paper 2 you must keep your tenses under control when you tell what happened. This course shows you which clues to look for.

items: A French verb changes its form according to its subject (je, tu, il, elle, nous, vous, ils, elles).
Avoir and être are the auxiliary verbs that build the compound tenses.
A past participle is the form used after an auxiliary, such as mangé, fini or vendu.

sections.titre: Reading the clues before you choose a verb form
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Read the clues before you choose

A French verb form carries two pieces of information: who does the action (the subject) and when it happens (the tense or mood). In a gap-fill sentence, find the subject first, then look for the time clues: a time word (*hier*, *demain*, *chaque jour*), another verb, or a clause with *si*.

### The main forms

| Form | Use | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Présent | now, general truths, habits | *Nous mangeons du riz.* (We are eating rice.) |
| Passé composé | a finished action in the past (avoir or être + past participle) | *Hier, j'ai visité le marché.* (Yesterday I visited the market.) |
| Imparfait | description, background, repeated habit in the past | *Il pleuvait et les rues étaient vides.* (It was raining and the streets were empty.) |
| Plus-que-parfait | an action finished before another past action (imparfait of avoir or être + past participle) | *Quand je suis arrivé, le bus était déjà parti.* (When I arrived, the bus had already left.) |
| Futur simple | what will happen | *Demain, nous irons au village.* (Tomorrow we shall go to the village.) |
| Conditionnel présent | a wish, a polite request, the result of an unlikely condition | *Je voudrais un verre d'eau.* (I would like a glass of water.) |
| Subjonctif présent | after expressions of need, wish, feeling or doubt | *Il faut que tu viennes.* (You must come.) |

### Sentences with si (if)

| Clause with si | Result clause | Example |
|---|---|---|
| présent | futur simple | *Si tu étudies, tu réussiras.* (If you study, you will succeed.) |
| imparfait | conditionnel présent | *Si tu étudiais, tu réussirais.* (If you studied, you would succeed.) |
| plus-que-parfait | conditionnel passé | *Si tu avais étudié, tu aurais réussi.* (If you had studied, you would have succeeded.) |

Never put a future or a conditional right after *si* when it means 'if'.

variantes.nom: Telling a story in the past
variantes.quand_utiliser: When a Paper 2 task asks you to tell what happened
variantes.contenu_markdown: Use the passé composé for the events that move the story forward, the imparfait for the weather, feelings, the state of things and habits, and the plus-que-parfait for what had happened earlier. Keep the same time frame from beginning to end. *Il était tard et il faisait nuit quand nous avons quitté l'hôpital. Le médecin avait déjà examiné ma sœur.* (It was late and dark when we left the hospital. The doctor had already examined my sister.) After a verb in the past, a second verb that gives the background or the ability at the same moment is usually in the imparfait: *Elle a donné tout ce qu'elle avait.* (She gave everything she had.) In reported speech after a past verb, the future becomes the conditionnel: *Il a promis qu'il viendrait.* (He promised that he would come.)

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the blank follows il faut que, vouloir que, bien que, pour que, avant que or il est important que
variantes.contenu_markdown: The subjonctif is used when the two clauses have different subjects. Compare *Je veux partir* (one subject, infinitive) with *Je veux que tu partes* (two subjects, subjonctif). For regular -er verbs the forms are like the présent for je, tu, il and ils (*que je parle*, *qu'ils parlent*) and like the imparfait for nous and vous (*que nous parlions*). Learn the irregular ones: *être* → *que je sois*; *avoir* → *que j'aie*; *aller* → *que j'aille*; *faire* → *que je fasse*; *pouvoir* → *que je puisse*; *savoir* → *que je sache*; *venir* → *que tu viennes*. *Bien qu'il soit malade, il travaille.* (Although he is ill, he works.) After *savoir que* or *penser que* in the affirmative, use the indicative: *Je sais qu'il est là.* (I know he is there.)

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the sentence contains a word that fixes the time
variantes.contenu_markdown: Hier, la semaine dernière, il y a deux jours: passé composé. Autrefois, chaque jour, souvent, d'habitude (in a story about the past): imparfait. Demain, bientôt, l'année prochaine: futur simple. Déjà before another past event: plus-que-parfait. Maintenant, en ce moment: présent. Always check that the clue fits the whole sentence, not only one word.

sections.enonce_markdown:
Si nous ____ plus tôt, nous n'aurions pas raté le car.
A) partons   B) partirons   C) étions partis   D) partirions

etapes.action: Read the clause that has no blank.
etapes.justification: The verb in the result clause fixes the pattern that the si-clause must follow.
A conditionnel passé in the result clause goes with a plus-que-parfait after si.
Partirons (futur) and partirions (conditionnel) never follow si meaning 'if'. Partons (présent) would need a future in the result clause.
etapes.resultat_markdown: A, B and D are rejected.

etapes.action: Check the form of option C.
etapes.justification: Partir uses être in the compound tenses, so the plus-que-parfait of nous is nous étions partis.
The meaning must be logical: the missing of the bus is the result of not leaving early.
etapes.resultat_markdown: *Si nous étions partis plus tôt, nous n'aurions pas raté le car.* Answer **C**.

sections.conclusion_markdown: The answer is **C) étions partis**. The sentence means: 'If we had left earlier, we would not have missed the bus.' The plus-que-parfait after *si* matches the conditionnel passé of the result clause.

items.erreur_markdown: A student writes: *Si j'aurais de l'argent, j'achèterais un téléphone.* (incorrect)
items.pourquoi_faux: The student put a conditional after si. After si meaning 'if', the conditional is never used.
items.correction_markdown: *Si j'avais de l'argent, j'achèterais un téléphone.* (If I had money, I would buy a phone.)

items.erreur_markdown: A student writes: *Hier, nous allons au marché.* (incorrect)
items.pourquoi_faux: Hier points to the past, but the student used the présent.
items.correction_markdown: *Hier, nous sommes allés au marché.* (Yesterday we went to the market.)

items.erreur_markdown: A student writes: *Il faut que tu viens demain.* (incorrect)
items.pourquoi_faux: Il faut que must be followed by the subjonctif. Viens is the indicative.
items.correction_markdown: *Il faut que tu viennes demain.* (You must come tomorrow.)

items.erreur_markdown: A student writes: *Quand je suis arrivé, le match a déjà commencé.* (incorrect)
items.pourquoi_faux: The match began before the arrival, so the earlier action needs the plus-que-parfait.
items.correction_markdown: *Quand je suis arrivé, le match avait déjà commencé.* (When I arrived, the match had already started.)

items.erreur_markdown: A student writes: *Bien qu'il est malade, il va à l'école.* (incorrect)
items.pourquoi_faux: Bien que is always followed by the subjonctif.
items.correction_markdown: *Bien qu'il soit malade, il va à l'école.* (Although he is ill, he goes to school.)

items.enonce_markdown:
Demain, nous ____ chez notre grand-mère.
A) allions   B) irons   C) sommes allés   D) irions
items.solution_markdown: *Demain* (tomorrow) points to the future. Answer **B) irons**. *Allions* is the imparfait, *sommes allés* is the passé composé and *irions* is the conditionnel.

items.enonce_markdown:
Il faut que vous ____ à l'heure demain matin.
A) êtes   B) serez   C) soyez   D) seriez
items.solution_markdown: *Il faut que* is followed by the subjonctif. The subjonctif of être for vous is *vous soyez*. Answer **C) soyez**. *Êtes* is the indicative, *serez* the future and *seriez* the conditional.

items.enonce_markdown:
(a) Si la pluie avait cessé, nous ____ au match.
A) irions   B) sommes allés   C) serions allés   D) irons

(b) Quand nous sommes arrivés à la gare, le train ____ déjà quitté le quai.
A) avait   B) a   C) aura   D) aurait

(c) Write two sentences in French about a visit to the market last Saturday: one that describes the weather or the crowd, and one that tells what you bought.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) *Si* + plus-que-parfait (*avait cessé*) needs the conditionnel passé in the result clause: *nous serions allés* (aller takes être). Answer **C**.

(b) We arrived in the past and the train left before that, so the plus-que-parfait is needed: *avait quitté*. Answer **A**.

(c) Model answer: *Il faisait chaud et il y avait beaucoup de monde. J'ai acheté des légumes et du poisson.* (It was hot and there were many people. I bought vegetables and fish.) Award a mark for the imparfait in the description, a mark for the passé composé with the right auxiliary in the event, and a mark for correct spelling and accents.

items_markdown: A verb form carries who and when: find the subject, then the time clues, before you choose.
Passé composé = finished event; imparfait = description, background and habit; plus-que-parfait = what had happened earlier.
With si meaning 'if': présent → futur; imparfait → conditionnel présent; plus-que-parfait → conditionnel passé. Never a future or conditional right after si.
Il faut que, vouloir que, bien que, pour que and avant que are followed by the subjonctif; learn sois, aie, aille, fasse, puisse, sache.
In a Paper 2 narrative keep one time frame and mix the past tenses on purpose, not by accident.
